subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should this canonical anti-drift tracker become a narrow core runner guard, merge into the structured lifecycle contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/17213, or stay blocked on a concrete reproduction before implementation?
rationale: The source gap is real enough to keep open, but the requested enforcement changes runtime policy, persistence, config/feature-flag surface, telemetry, and false-positive behavior; automation cannot choose that product contract safely.

options.title: Unify With Lifecycle Contract
options.body: Treat artifact evidence, escalation timers, blocker state, and no-idle-after-green as acceptance criteria for the structured begin/exec/commit-or-abort contract instead of adding a separate progress state machine.

options.title: Narrow To One Reproduced Guard
options.body: Keep this issue open but require a concrete current-main trace, then implement the smallest runner guard for that drift mode only.

options.title: Reject Broad Enforcement
options.body: Close or narrow the issue if maintainers decide artifact-gated status/timer enforcement is too heavy for core and existing terminal/liveness safeguards are sufficient.

recommendation.title: Unify With Lifecycle Contract
recommendation.body: Treat artifact evidence, escalation timers, blocker state, and no-idle-after-green as acceptance criteria for the structured begin/exec/commit-or-abort contract instead of adding a separate progress state machine.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest visible product-contract review signal on the overlapping lifecycle issue and recent history on adjacent runner guard files.
